title: Polaris Distributed SQL Query Engine
purpose: Trace SQL compilation, distributed task planning, scheduling, stateless execution, and cell-based access to durable storage.
accessibleSummary: SQL enters a front end and two-phase optimizer. DQP turns the plan into a task DAG. Finite-state orchestration and a global scheduler place work on stateless compute. Tasks operate over data cells whose durable state remains in remote storage.
longDescription: Polaris separates SQL compilation from distributed execution. The optimizer selects physical distribution and movement. DQP divides plans into maximal tasks connected as a DAG. Hierarchical finite-state machines manage progress and retry. A global workload graph schedules tasks onto stateless SQL compute. Cell abstractions connect those tasks to partitioned and hash-distributed data in durable remote storage.

nodes.label: SQL front end
nodes.summary: The SQL front end parses and optimizes a query before distributed execution.
nodes.detail: The SQL front end parses and optimizes a query before distributed execution. Bind names, optimize expressions, and produce a plan.
nodes.whyItMatters: A plan ready for distributed physical planning depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: The SQL frontend optimizes requests and passes plans to DQP.

inputs: T-SQL request, schema metadata, and statistics
processing: Bind names, optimize expressions, and produce a plan
outputs: A plan ready for distributed physical planning
drill.example: A grouped sales query is compiled before any backend task runs.
failureModes: Stale statistics lead to a costly distribution choice

nodes.label: Distributed optimizer
nodes.summary: A second planning phase chooses distribution properties and minimizes data movement.
nodes.detail: A second planning phase chooses distribution properties and minimizes data movement. Enumerate distributed alternatives and add required move operators.
nodes.whyItMatters: A valid distributed physical plan depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Polaris performs distributed cost-based planning and injects redistribution or broadcast enforcers.

inputs: Logical optimizer search space and data distributions
processing: Enumerate distributed alternatives and add required move operators
drill.example: A small dimension is broadcast instead of repartitioning a large fact table.
failureModes: Bad estimates choose a broadcast too large for available memory

nodes.label: Task DAG
nodes.summary: DQP divides the physical plan into tasks linked by dataflow and precedence.
nodes.detail: DQP divides the physical plan into tasks linked by dataflow and precedence. Fuse compatible operators and cut tasks at blocking movement boundaries.
nodes.whyItMatters: A directed acyclic graph of executable tasks depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: A Polaris plan becomes a DAG of task templates whose edges encode dataflow and precedence.

inputs: Distributed physical operators and cell collections
processing: Fuse compatible operators and cut tasks at blocking movement boundaries
outputs: A directed acyclic graph of executable tasks
drill.example: Aligned joins remain one task while a hash redistribution creates a boundary.
failureModes: Excessive movement produces slow blocking stages

nodes.label: FSM orchestration
nodes.summary: Hierarchical state machines track query, template, and task progress and retry.
nodes.detail: Hierarchical state machines track query, template, and task progress and retry. Advance states, log transitions, retry transient task failures.
nodes.whyItMatters: Resumable and reproducible query execution depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Polaris orchestrates execution with hierarchical finite-state machines and task-level retry.

inputs: Task DAG, state transitions, and failure signals
processing: Advance states, log transitions, retry transient task failures
drill.example: One failed task is retried without restarting every completed task.
failureModes: A persistent data error is repeatedly misclassified as transient

nodes.label: Global workload scheduler
nodes.summary: A workload graph schedules tasks across concurrent queries by multidimensional resource demand.
nodes.detail: A workload graph schedules tasks across concurrent queries by multidimensional resource demand. Select eligible tasks and place them on available compute.
nodes.whyItMatters: Concurrent task assignments across the pool depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: The scheduler unions active task DAGs and places tasks using CPU, memory, and disk demand.

inputs: Ready tasks, node resources, and active-query DAGs
processing: Select eligible tasks and place them on available compute
outputs: Concurrent task assignments across the pool
drill.example: Root-near tasks are prioritized to release shared resources sooner.
failureModes: Resource pressure delays tasks while callers assume fixed latency

nodes.label: Stateless compute pool
nodes.summary: Compute nodes run task templates while durable state remains external.
nodes.detail: Compute nodes run task templates while durable state remains external. Execute encoded SQL operators and materialize output cells.
nodes.whyItMatters: Task results and updated cache locality depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Polaris externalizes durable data, metadata, and logs; compute retains only rebuildable caches.

inputs: Scheduled task, input cells, and local cache state
processing: Execute encoded SQL operators and materialize output cells
outputs: Task results and updated cache locality
drill.example: A replacement node re-reads persisted cells after another node fails.
failureModes: Scale-out nodes start cold and temporarily lose cache locality

nodes.label: Data cells and storage
nodes.summary: Two-dimensional cells connect partition pruning and hash distribution to durable data.
nodes.detail: Two-dimensional cells connect partition pruning and hash distribution to durable data. Prune partitions, select hash buckets, and read or write cell collections.
nodes.whyItMatters: Storage-agnostic inputs and durable task outputs depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Datasets are grids of partitioned and hash-distributed cells used as DQP units.

inputs: Partition predicates, distribution keys, and stored table data
processing: Prune partitions, select hash buckets, and read or write cell collections
outputs: Storage-agnostic inputs and durable task outputs
drill.example: A date predicate prunes partitions while customer hash spreads work across nodes.
failureModes: Skew concentrates cells and computation on too few nodes
